title: Sen. Lindsey Graham dies at 71 after ‘brief and sudden illness’
---
<p>WASHINGTON — Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., who was elected to the Senate in 2003 and was a close political ally of President Donald Trump, has died, his office confirmed early Sunday. He was 71.</p>
<figure><img alt="NBC News Icon" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,"/></figure>

<figure><img alt="arrow" src="https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/rockcms/2026-01/arrow-f55fa5.svg"/></figure>
<p>Graham died Saturday night “from a brief and sudden illness,” his office said in a statement.</p>
<p>“Senator Graham’s family appreciates prayers at this time and asks for privacy during this incredibly difficult period,” the statement continued.</p>
<p>Graham was chairman of the Senate Budget Committee and was seeking a fifth six-year Senate term in November. He was one of the most well-known members of the chamber and a key voice within the party on defense and international affairs.</p>
<p>Emergency personnel responded to a call for “cardiac arrest” at Graham’s Capitol Hill home on Saturday night, according to police scanner audio obtained by NBC News.</p>
<p>Photographs reviewed by NBC News show that paramedics carried a person on a stretcher from Graham’s home to an awaiting ambulance. Police cars and fire trucks were also on site.</p>

<p>Graham was fresh off a trip to Kyiv, Ukraine, where he <a href="https://x.com/ZelenskyyUa/status/2075622796819128501?s=20">met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy</a> on Friday. He had been scheduled to appear on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday.</p>
<p>His death comes as fellow Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/mitch-mcconnell-remains-hospitalized-three-weeks-rcna353183">remains in the hospital </a>after paramedics responded to a call at a known residence last month for an individual experiencing cardiac arrest.</p>
<p>A McConnell spokesperson has said the former GOP majority leader is continuing to recover, but his team has not provided further details about his condition.</p>
